blocks.text:
After breakfast, take a boat trip to the floating Uros Islands.

High in the Andes, Titicaca is considered the world's highest navigable lake.

The Uros Islands are built from reeds. The cold waters of Titicaca stretch towards a distant mountain horizon, while the islands seem like a separate, human-made world. They are home to Aymara people who preserve traditional occupations and aspects of everyday life.

Reeds are used for the foundations of the islands, as well as for houses and boats. Fishing remains an important activity, and residents make souvenirs for visitors. Bright ponchos, layered skirts and distinctive hats are notable features of their clothing.

After the tour, return to Puno and transfer to your hotel.
